title: Disability Compensation Restoration After Reduction: Restoration Months and Amount Standing Paid
content:
**Rule.** The restoration on a Disability Compensation award is the entitlement the award now carries for the restoration months, less what stands paid for those months, and never less than nothing; it is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Restoration months.** The restoration months are the whole months elapsed from the restoration's start date to today, less one for the current month.

**Start date.** The restoration's start date is the date the reduced rate took effect — the effective date on the most recent rating decision implementing the reduction.

**What stands paid.** What stands paid for the restoration months is the gross of every monthly payment, replacement and past-due release issued on the award within that many whole months before today — that is, issued fewer whole months before today than the number of restoration months — less the gross of every payment that came back within the same months.

**Entitlement.** The entitlement for each restoration month is the veteran-alone rate of the award's combined rating, as the Disability Compensation rate table gives it for the tier the award now carries.

**Worked example (hypothetical award reduced from 70 percent to 50 percent and now again carrying Disability Compensation (70% Combined Rating); today 15 September 2026).**

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Reduced rate took effect | 1 March 2026 |
| Whole months to today | 6; less one for the current month: 5 restoration months |
| Entitlement | 1808.45 multiplied by 5: 9042.25 |
| Stands paid | Monthly payments issued 1 May, 1 June, 1 July, 1 August and 1 September 2026 (fewer than 5 whole months before today), 1132.90 each: 5664.50; nothing came back |
| Restoration | 9042.25 less 5664.50: 3377.75 |

A monthly payment issued on 1 April 2026 lies 5 whole months before today and is not among the payments standing for the restoration months.
